prompt: Use case: illustration-story. Asset type: a production atlas of circular illustrated tokens for Creation, an original elemental myth about making a vast living world. The reference is the APPROVED STYLE AND CONTINUITY anchor, not a sheet to copy unchanged. Paint new subjects in exactly that family: luminous opaque gouache, selective fine ink contours, strong simplified silhouettes readable at 64px; deep lapis interiors, jade and turquoise, burnt ochre, muted coral, warm ivory light, very narrow ivory-gold rims. Not glossy coins or flat generic pictograms. Each icon is a complete perfect CIRCLE with opaque painted interior and transparent empty space outside. Center each circle in its own equal grid cell, circle diameter 80 percent of the shorter cell side, generous empty gutters. Absolutely no letters, names, numbers, grid lines, labels, UI, watermark or cast shadows outside circles. No modern laboratory hardware, books, houses or buildings. Only the specified object inside each circle, with a simple dark ground or essential local context. Tiny details must not carry the meaning. Related states should differ in structure, not merely colour. Follow item order exactly, left to right, top to bottom. Exactly 6 circles in 3 columns and 2 rows. Landscape atlas. Exact cell subjects: CELL 1, New question: A young learner lifts an open hand toward a different star beyond the Moon-and-tide pattern in the sand while an older teacher pauses and turns to follow the new direction. Distinguish: The learner extends inquiry beyond the received pattern; no question mark, certificate or passive reception. CELL 2, Children's chorus: Three children of visibly different small heights sing together on the cave's dry ledge, sharing the inherited two ivory arcs and the new rising coral ending; a taller adult listens at the far edge. Distinguish: Children collectively perform the changed motif, rather than adult chorus, solo revision or spoken lesson. CELL 3, Dormant seeds: Three intact dark-coated seeds rest protected beneath a curled dry leaf and a thin layer of cold soil, while a pale frost edge lies above them; no root has emerged. Distinguish: Living seeds waiting through unfavorable conditions, not stored food cache, dead grains or active germination. CELL 4, Scattered seeds: Several familiar dark-coated seeds lie well separated across new ochre ground, with one near an animal footprint and another beneath a distant fruit branch; none has sprouted yet. Distinguish: Arrived seeds spread across multiple places, not winged airborne seeds, carrying action or one sheltered cluster. CELL 5, Young grove: Four fresh jade saplings of differing heights establish on an open ochre slope, with visible seed coats at one root and clear space between their small crowns. Distinguish: New grove on open ground with no catastrophe logs; larger than a seedling and smaller than a distant established forest. CELL 6, Forest beyond the horizon: A near grove releases a few small winged seeds toward a distant green ridge where additional young tree crowns disappear beyond the circle's far curve; a small open human hand remains low at the edge. Distinguish: Continuing establishment beyond view dominates, with the hand releasing rather than arranging; no living great browsers or final perfection emblem. Keep the common circle size and painted finish. Anatomical lineages matter: insects have six legs, birds feathered wings, bats membranous finger-supported wings. A depicted early cell is a symbolic magnified view, not a modern laboratory slide. The world is not Earth's recognizable map. People, if listed, have varied warm earth-brown complexions, simplified features and no modern objects. Never add people, plants or animals to a subject that predates them. Do not draw the subject names.
